Intravenous doses for conventional and lipid formulations of amphotericin B similar to those in adults have been found to be safe and effective in children and neonates with candidiasis. For neonates with se- vere disease, dose increments of conventional amphotericin B every 12 hours have been given and daily doses up to 1.5 mg/kg tolerated. For prophylaxis of neonatal intestinal candidiasis con- ventional amphotericin B solution 100 mg is given orally once daily. Although the most appropriate dose of lipid formulations of amphotericin B for low-birth-weight preterm infants has yet to be firmly established reports suggest that they may be safe and effective at doses similar to those used in adults, relative to body- weight.1-3 For information on the pharmacokinetics and doses in children and neonates, see, above. 1.
